prose.summary: Translators carry meaning, tone and practical intent from one language into another for a defined audience. They research terminology, revise text and protect consistency across many pieces of content. The live sample also includes interpreters and localization specialists, which are related but distinct roles.
prose.day_to_day: The work includes reading source material, researching terms, drafting, revising and resolving ambiguous passages with clients or editors. Localization adds product, gaming or sports context and consistency across releases. Interpreting appears in the titles but happens in real time rather than through written revision. Quality control matters because fluent wording can still be wrong.
prose.work_environment: Most openings in the current sample are remote, often freelance or contract, across many languages. Sign-language and live interpretation can require scheduled presence or video sessions. Work volume and deadlines vary with projects rather than following one stable employer pattern.
prose.getting_in: Work only into languages you can handle at professional depth and choose a domain where terminology can be verified. Build samples with source context, translation choices and revision notes. Writing, localization and subject knowledge matter more than literal word substitution.
prose.ladder: Early translators handle defined content under review. Responsibility grows toward specialized domains, terminology management, editing, localization quality or project leadership. The path can branch into interpretation, localization, copywriting or language-data work.
prose.suits: This work fits people who notice register, ambiguity and context and can revise without treating the first fluent sentence as finished. It requires tolerance for solitary detail and variable contract demand. It is a poor fit if speed matters more than verified meaning.
prose.misconceptions: Translation is not replacing each word with its dictionary equivalent, and fluency alone does not guarantee professional accuracy. Domain knowledge, research and revision decide whether the text works.
prose.who_qualifies: Writers, interpreters, localization staff and subject specialists with professional language command bring adjacent foundations. They need translation samples and quality-control evidence. Casual bilingual ability is not enough.
prose.what_the_numbers_miss: Listings cannot show source quality, revision expectations or whether the client pays for terminology research. Those conditions determine both quality and workload.

steps.how: Work into the language where you can control tone, grammar and domain-specific meaning at professional depth.
Build terminology and source knowledge in legal, medical, technical, gaming or another target field.
Show the source context, difficult choices and revisions rather than presenting only the final translated text.
Use terminology records, second-pass review and consistency checks before delivery.

prose.tools: Translation, localization, technical writing, general writing, copywriting, NLP, Excel, machine learning and quality control lead the live evidence. Tool choice varies by client, but terminology and revision discipline remain central.

faq.q: how do you become a translator?
faq.a: Choose a professional language direction and domain, then build annotated samples that show research, judgment and revision. Fluency alone is not a complete portfolio.
Yes. Most current openings are remote, although live and sign-language interpretation can require scheduled presence or video work.

faq.q: what is the difference between translation and interpretation?
faq.a: Translation works with written content and allows revision, while interpretation transfers spoken or signed meaning in real time. The skills overlap but the operating conditions differ.
